## 8. Models

<!-- models:start (generated by tools/process_models.mjs; edit outside these markers) -->

### Anaglyph 3D (`lumenary:anaglyph-3d`, models this process)

_From: 19th century stereoscopy; when: 1850s onward, popular in the 1950s and 2010s; works best on: Landscapes and scenes with a clear foreground and background._

Your two eyes see a scene from slightly different places, and near things shift more between the two views than far things do. A single photograph carries no depth, so the program guesses one, shifts each eye’s view sideways by it, and then colours the two views so that a pair of coloured glasses separates them again for each eye.

**How it is made, as the model does it:**

1. Guess a depth map from a heavily blurred lightness: bright is near, dark is near, a ground plane in which lower means nearer, or a mix.
2. Shift each pixel sideways by its depth minus the focus depth, up to 46 pixels.
3. Look up the left view at x minus the shift, and the right view at x plus the shift, with bilinear sampling.
4. Pixels at the focus plane do not shift and sit at the screen, while nearer and farther ones separate in opposite directions.
5. Combine the two views by the glasses: red from the left and green and blue from the right for red and cyan, and so on, optionally keeping some original colour.

**The maths:**

$$s=(d-d_f)\cdot 46\,\kappa\,\frac{W}{800},\qquad d=\begin{cases}L_b & \text{bright is near}\\ 1-L_b & \text{dark is near}\\ y/H & \text{ground}\\ 0.55\,L_b+0.45\,y/H & \text{mixed}\end{cases}$$

_Disparity: d is the guessed depth from the blurred luminance L_b, d_f the focus plane and κ the depth slider._ (written for this model: specific)

$$\mathbf a=C(x-s,\ y),\qquad \mathbf b=C(x+s,\ y),\qquad \mathbf a'=l_a+k\,(\mathbf a-l_a)$$

_The two views (left a, right b) and the keep-colour mixing with each view’s own luminance l._ (primitives: coordinate-warp, saturation-adjust)

$$(R,G,B)_{\text{red-cyan}}=\big(a'_R,\ \ b'_G,\ \ b'_B\big)$$

_What the glasses combine; for the other pairs the channels are assigned as described above._ (primitives: channel-mix)

**Dials:** `depth` (Depth) = 60 [0 to 100]; `src` (How depth is guessed) = "mix" (bright, dark, ground, mix); `focus` (Focus plane) = 45 [0 to 100]; `glasses` (Glasses) = "rc" (rc, mg, ab); `keep` (Keep original colour) = 65 [0 to 100].

**History:** Charles Wheatstone described the stereoscope in 1838, and Wilhelm Rollmann made the first anaglyphs in 1853 by printing two views in complementary colours. Louis Ducos du Hauron patented the process for photographs in 1891. Red and cyan 3D appeared in books, comics and cinema in the twentieth century, and again in the 2010s on early home 3D.
